message.abstract: <jats:p>Unsupervised anomaly detection, a fundamental challenge in computer vision, requires accurately identifying and segmenting anomalous regions using only normal samples for training. However, the domain gap between pre-training and anomaly detection data, the redundancy of normal prototypes in the memory bank, and the randomness of the anomaly suppression mechanism remain key challenges limiting the performance of tasks such as multi-class anomaly detection and few-shot detection. To address these challenges, we propose ProtoFocus - a novel framework based on compact normal prototypes and implicit anomaly suppression. The framework consists of three core components: the Differential Complementary Adaptor (DCA) alleviates data gaps in pre-trained models through multi-level feature complementation learning, effectively bridging domain discrepancies with anomaly data; the Token-Channel Adaptive Normal Prototype (TCANP) Distiller employs cross-attention mechanisms and token-channel diversity losses optimization to construct geometrically compact and semantically robust normal prototypes that surpass conventional memory banks in representational capability; and the Sparse Mask Decoder (SMD) utilizes sparse correlations between normal prototypes and input features to precisely localize and mask potential anomalous regions, significantly improving both reconstruction quality and decoding efficiency. Extensive experiments on MVTec AD, VisA, MPDD, and BTAD datasets demonstrate that ProtoFocus achieves state-of-the-art performance in anomaly detection and localization across few-shot, single-class, and multi-class scenarios, exhibiting superior generalization capability.</jats:p>
title: ProtoFocus: Industrial Anomaly Detection with Prototype distillation and Latent Inhibition
